lanes.PROBLEM: Find open-source solutions to problems FTN already has an active ticket/roadmap item for.
lanes.CAPABILITY: Find emerging open-source capability FTN could use even without a current ticket -- not ranked primarily by star count.
lanes.ARCHITECTURE: Find infrastructure that could replace a planned build or become shared FTN infrastructure -- "what are we about to build that already exists?"

queries.why: Improve browser-local creation, export and interoperability without uploading a creator's audio.
Improve processing, analysis and local-audio workflows while keeping streamed media rights-safe.
Strengthen the FTN dispatcher, provenance and Caribbean-relevant intelligence interfaces.
Improve trust, performance, accessibility and FTN-owned data interfaces across nodes.
Scan for real capability FTN doesn't have an open ticket for yet, so ibis's own current roadmap isn't the only lens FTN sees new capability through.
Before FTN builds a new subsystem from scratch, check whether real, licensable infrastructure already solves it.
Find practical open infrastructure for guaranteed answer-path continuity without making one hosted provider a single point of failure.
Track deployable voice, transcription and rendering systems with clear model and output licences.
YouTube is a discovery signal only; every candidate must be verified against its primary repository, documentation and licence before ibis recommends it.
Continuously find standardized tools ibis could connect through its governed capability and permission boundary.
Support product identification, supplier comparison, Trinidad landed-cost analysis and evidence-backed import planning.
Strengthen eligibility extraction, evidence checklists, deadlines and approval-controlled application preparation.
Support rights-aware music analysis, metadata, release planning and reusable Caribbean music workflows.
Find modular commerce, campaign and service components that ibis can orchestrate without replacing FTN ownership or WAM.
Give every ibis workflow a common, privacy-conscious intake path for files, photos, audio, video and URLs.
